request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

agent.result_text:
The claims export is in and all 4 `bin/e2e` tests pass on the final code. A separate TypeScript check didn't run because the compiler isn't installed here, but the build inside `bin/e2e` succeeded.

**What it does:** a new "Export claims (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) sits next to the people export, in `src/main/frontend/features/claims/export.slot.tsx`. It downloads `claims-<sheet>.csv`:
- The header is `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then one line per claim.
- People come in list order, and retired people are included whether shown or not.
- Each person's claims are oldest first. The server sends them newest first, so the export reverses them.
- Number, due, status and period are worked out the same way the claim row on screen does it, so an empty number or period and `n/a` come out exactly as shown.
- It uses the same quoting as the people export, and every line ends with `\n`.

**One change to existing code:** I exported the `csvValue` helper from `features/people/export.slot.tsx` so both exports share the same quoting.

It's front-end only. The page already had all the claim data, so the server and stored data didn't need to change.
